## Glossary

**backfill**  
`archive route --backfill [--dry-run]`: plan every unplanned session, parents first.

**checked**  
A plan whose every window passed the sensitivity pass (sensitivityKey); only checked plans publish.

**decision-receipts**  
The run directory planner runs live in; collectors exclude it, so the planner is never captured.

**delta**  
A pass over the prior plan plus entries added since.

**due**  
A session marked for planning: new content after a pause, a route: change, a parent or subagent plan change, an organization or map change.

**firstEntryId / lastEntryId**  
The source entry range a part's lineage carries.

**held**  
A plan or part kept personal for review: failed run, invalid plan, or a hold.

**heldForReview**  
Entries held from personal-only talk under hold, unapplied redactions and parts the planner marked held.

**part**  
A contiguous entry range stored as its own row `<sessionId>#part-<first entry id>`, lineage kind `part`.

**partOf**  
A part row's link to the session it was cut from.

**prune**  
An entry the plan drops from a part as irrelevant.

**redaction**  
A byte-exact quoted span replaced with `[redacted: <reason>]` wherever it appears in the part.

**REDACTION_REASONS**  
The closed reason set: coworker, career, personal-life, investor, secret, other.

**route agent**  
The `com.inixiative.archive.route` unit running `route --watch --limit N` (30 by default).

**route:<organization>**  
A person's tag edit deciding ownership; `route:personal` keeps the session here.

**ROUTE_PROMPT**  
The planner's charter; with ROUTE_BASE_INSTRUCTIONS, SENSITIVITY_PROMPT and the model it makes routeKey.

**routeKey**  
Hash of the charters and model; a plan made under another key is re-planned.

**routing plan**  
A session's parts, their organizations, prunes, redactions, confidence and rationale; its own RoutingPlan record.

**routing-parts**  
Class: partSnapshot, part ids and lineage, redactText with the closed REDACTION_REASONS set.

**routing-planner**  
Class: ROUTE_PROMPT, parsePlan, validatePlan, scheduling, re-planning, backfill, plan records and review.

**sensitivity pass**  
A second Sonnet-low call per publishing part; can only add redactions or a hold; `route --no-sensitivity` turns it off.

**sticky**  
Prunes, redactions and sensitive personal parts carried across re-plans until `route reset`.

**validatePlan**  
Internal check of a proposal against evidence; it narrows, never widens.

**window**  
300k characters (ROUTE_WINDOW_CHARS); a longer session plans one window a pass.

## 1. What this Warden covers

The routing planner: a Sonnet run on the host that cuts each session into parts and names the organizations whose work each part is, the code that validates every plan (it can only narrow), scheduling, re-planning and backfill, the review queue, and the part rows with their redactions.

## 2. The domain

Apps run the planner with the CLI: `archive route --watch` (or the installed `route` agent, declared with `archive agents router`) wakes every two minutes, sends the project map and plans due sessions a window (300k characters) at a time; `archive route --backfill [--dry-run]` plans every session with no plan yet. Another process that plans goes through ArchiveStore.routingDue/routingInput/recordPlan (session-store) or ArchiveClient's routingDue()/routingInput()/recordPlan() (running-the-archive). planSession, runRouting, runBackfill, validatePlan, publishedParts and the Sonnet runner claudeRouteModel are internal to src/route.ts and src/suggest-claude.ts: name them only to maintainers.

Every proposal is checked in code before anything routes: a closed organization set plus `personal`, ordered disjoint parts, an organization only with evidence in the part, the session's start project or a person's `route:<organization>` tag, byte-exact redactions with a reason from the closed set (coworker, career, personal-life, investor, secret, other), foreign entries following their own session. A failed run, unparseable answer or invalid plan is held for review and changes nothing that publishes; confidence orders the queue and never gates. `archive route plans`, `review --id` and `reset --id` (routing/plans, routing/review, routing/reset) are the queue; sticky prunes, redactions and sensitive personal parts survive re-plans until reset. The sensitivity pass adds a second check per publishing part that can only remove.

Parts: ArchiveStore.applyParts writes each part as its own local row (lineage kind `part` with firstEntryId/lastEntryId, partOf, only its organizations' project: tags and every run: tag, never tool activity) built by partSnapshot with redactText replacing every echo of a redacted span; both are internal. Only parts publish, never whole sessions. Not here: the organizations, evidence and personalSpans policy (routing-organizations); delivering parts, deletes at destinations, cleanup and Kingdom (destinations-and-sync); the isolated subscription runner itself (tags-and-tagger); the RoutingPlan table and ArchiveStore (session-store).

| **partSnapshot** | maintainers changing what a part holds (internal) | app code (ArchiveStore.applyParts) |
| **redactText** | maintainers changing span replacement (internal) | app code (redactions apply in applyParts) |
| **Routing part rows** | reading parts: pass parts include or only | listing sessions (parts are hidden by default) |
| **Publish parts, never whole sessions** | deciding what may go to a destination | unplanned or held sessions (nothing publishes) |

| Problem | Use | Read | Signs you're bypassing it |
|---|---|---|---|
| while changing what a routed part snapshot contains; maintainer change to part tags and lineage; I'll slice the session's entries into a new snapshot | **partSnapshot** · primitive · internal, not importable (app code: `@inixiative/archive/store`) · source `src/parts.ts` — Internal to src/; not importable. App code goes through ArchiveStore.applyParts (@inixiative/archive/store). | docs/ROUTING.md § As built (2026-11-01, branch `feat/agentic-routing`) | `{ ...snapshot, entries: snapshot.entries.slice(` to make a part, keeping the session's references, tool activity and all its `project:` tags (README.md § Routing (a part holds only its organizations' project: tags, no recorded references, never tool activity)) |
| while changing how redacted spans are replaced; maintainer change to merging overlapping redactions; I'll string replace the sensitive sentence once | **redactText** · primitive · internal, not importable · source `src/parts.ts` — Internal to src/; not importable. Redaction applies when parts are built through ArchiveStore.applyParts. | — | `text.replace(span, '[redacted]')` on the one quoted entry, leaving later echoes of the span in the part (docs/ROUTING.md § As built (S2: echoes of a redacted span are replaced across the part)) |
| include parts when listing or searching; what does a part row hold and omit; show only the published slices of sessions | **Routing part rows** · primitive src/parts.ts partSnapshot, partSessionId — Parts stay out of listings and search unless parts: include\|only. | part 4 | — |
| send the whole session to the company archive; should an unplanned session publish anywhere; only the planned slices may leave this machine | **Publish parts, never whole sessions** · rule README.md § Routing — Only a session's parts per its routing plan publish; the whole session, unplanned sessions and held plans publish nowhere. | part 4 | publishing a row whose lineage is not `kind: 'part'`, or a session with no plan or a held plan (README.md § Routing) |

- *Also here, by name:* REDACTION_REASONS (`src/parts.ts`); partSessionId (`src/parts.ts`)

## 4. The specifics, in full

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#routing/routing-plans -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Routing › Routing plans (in "Archive")

##### Routing plans

**Routing plans.** The planner runs on the host (`archive route --watch`, the `route` agent beside the collectors): Claude Sonnet 5.5 at low effort, no tools, on primed, text-only sessions of the machine's **default (personal) Claude login**, whatever `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` says (`--claude-config-dir` names another login on purpose). Its runs are never captured: they run in `decision-receipts`, which collectors exclude, and a run that died has its directory and primed transcripts swept by the next. It reads the session stripped of tool activity, since its last plan (a delta, in windows for long sessions), with the session's **evidence**: what its tool calls wrote and read in which project, computed at ingest before the tool-activity strip and kept on the row only, never in a snapshot (the shell parser's write mode: redirections, `sed -i`, `cp`/`mv` targets, `mkdir`/`touch`/`rm`, git commands with `-C`/`--work-tree`, `gh pr|issue` with `-R`/`--repo`, mutating `gh api`, package-manager runs, Codex patches and `exec` cells with their own `workdir`, Foundry `tool` entries). The host sends its project map (every collector's roots and worktrees, and the GitHub repositories they push to) with `projects/set`; collectors send each session's working directory with its capture. Code validates every plan before it routes anything; it can narrow, never widen:
- organizations come from a closed set (the routing's, and `personal`), and parts are ordered, disjoint ranges of the entries planned;
- an organization is allowed for a part only when that part's own entries (or a subagent spawned in it) carry evidence for it, the session started in one of its projects, or a person decided it (a `route:<organization>` tag edit);
- every redaction quotes its entry byte for byte, for a listed reason (`coworker`, `career`, `personal-life`, `investor`, `secret`, `other`), and is replaced with `[redacted: <reason>]` wherever its text appears in the part;
- entries quoting another session (cross-session messages, subagent messages and results) publish only where that session is routed; a subagent reaches only where its parent's plan reached at the spawn, and waits for that plan;
- a person's `route:personal` keeps the session here; sensitive personal parts, prunes and redactions are sticky across re-plans (`route reset --id` drops a plan and its sticky decisions).
A failed run, an unparseable answer or a plan that fails validation is held for review and changes nothing that publishes; confidence orders the review queue and never gates. `route plans` lists held plans and those with redactions or low confidence a person has not read (`route review --id` marks one read); `--all` lists every plan.

**Going live.** `publish` in `destinations.json` (`archive publish on|off`) is the go-live switch, `off` by default: sessions are planned and plans validated and applied here, and sync only deletes leaked whole-session copies; nothing new publishes to an organization. Turn it on once plans pass review.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#routing/former-roots-re-planning-and-scheduling -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Routing › Former roots, re-planning and scheduling (in "Archive")

##### Former roots, re-planning and scheduling

**Former roots.** A collector in `agents.json` may name `formerRoots`: where its project's checkouts used to live (`~/Desktop/inixiative/template`). Evidence resolves paths there to the project; nothing is collected or routed from them. Codex rollouts Codex moved to `archived_sessions` are collected with the rest.

**Re-planning.** A plan made under another charter or model is re-planned with the model from the first entry, one window a pass, while the old plan keeps governing what publishes; its sticky prunes, redactions and sensitive personal entries carry over, and the new plan replaces it once it reaches the last entry. A session with no evidence for any organization holds without a model call.

**Scheduling.** `route --watch` wakes every two minutes, sends the project map, and plans the due sessions, at most `--concurrency` at once and at most `--limit` a wake (30 by default for the installed `route` agent, so a backfill's worth spreads across wakes). Only unplanned sessions and plans something marked due are read: new content (due once the session paused, about 30 minutes without a capture, or about an hour after its plan, staggered by up to ten minutes), a person's `route:` change, a parent's or subagent's plan changing, or a change to the organizations or project map (all at once; a plan with no new entries is re-applied and re-validated without a model call). A session longer than one window (300k characters) plans one window a pass. Exempt runs, superseded raw captures and parts received from another Archive are never planned. `archive agents router [--concurrency N]` declares the agent; `agents install` installs it with the collectors. The planner sees entries whole; one longer than a window is shown cut and can't publish unless pruned. A subagent whose spawn entry can't be found in its parent (Codex subagents, Claude subagents without meta) holds.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#routing/routing-over-http -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Routing › Routing over HTTP (in "Archive")

##### Routing over HTTP

The server manages routes over HTTP too, so Foundry can read and set them. Only Kingdom destinations are set this way, through the Signets `pair` collected; direct token destinations stay CLI-only.

| Action | Body | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `destinations/list` | `organizationId?` | `destinations`: each as `connect` reports it, with `delivered` (the organization's archives acknowledged at their latest digest) and `pending` |
| `organizations/list` | none | `organizations`: each `id` and its `projects` |
| `organizations/set` | `id`, `projects` | `organizations` |
| `organizations/remove` | `id` | `removed` |
| `destinations/libraries` | none | `paired`, and the `libraries` (`integrationId`, `resourceId`, `name`) the held Signets may write to |
| `destinations/connect` | `organizationId`, `integrationId`, `resourceId` | the saved destination, after Kingdom confirms `sessions.write` on the library (403 otherwise); an organization not declared yet is added with no projects |
| `destinations/remove` | `organizationId`, `integrationId`, `resourceId` | `removed` |
| `destinations/routes` | none | each archive (parts included) with its `partOf`, `organizations` and their destinations; nothing is sent |
| `destinations/sync` | none | one publication to every destination: `id`, `destination`, `status` (`published`, `unchanged`, `deleted`, `deferred …`, `failed …`) per archive and route |
| `routing/due` | `limit?` | sessions due for a plan, in planning order, with why |
| `routing/input` | `archiveId` | what the planner reads: the entries since the plan, their evidence, the plan so far, subagents, parent, organizations |
| `routing/record` | `archiveId`, `digest`, `through`, `key`, `by`, `proposal?` or `failure?`, `dryRun?` | `status` (`valid`, `held`, `stale`), `version`, `issues`, `notes`, the `parts` it publishes, `retired` |

`routing/plans` (`all?`, `limit?`), `routing/review` and `routing/reset` (`archiveId`) are the review queue's actions; they need no configuration. `@inixiative/archive/remote`'s `ArchiveClient` wraps these as `routingDue()`, `routingInput()`, `recordPlan()`, `routingPlans()`, `reviewPlan()` and `resetPlan()`, and `destinations()`, `libraries()`, `connectDestination()`, `removeDestination()`, `routes()` and `sync()`. The sync loop picks up changes within 30 seconds.

<!-- unit doc:docs/ROUTING.md#the-rule-one-paragraph -->
**Source:** `docs/ROUTING.md` § The rule, one paragraph (in "Archive routing: an agentic pass over each session artifact (spec v2, Aron 2026-11-01; built)")

#### The rule, one paragraph

Every session is captured locally and kept whole there (the personal Archive; local only for now). On the scheduler's cadence (Cadence, below), a **routing agent** (Sonnet 5.5 on the subscription, low effort, no tools, through the same isolated runner the tagger uses, its own run exempt from capture) reads the **stripped artifact**, i.e. the typed text, assistant text and events that survive the tool-activity strip, plus an **evidence table** the store computed at ingest, before the tool-activity strip, while the tool calls still existed: write targets and reads per organization (path → project by longest root → organization through Archive's org map: Zealot → UserEvidence, the `~/code/inixiative` container and its repos → inixiative, else personal), the start cwd, and references (repos, PRs, Linear keys). It returns a **routing plan**: zero or more **parts** (entry ranges; a whole session is one part), and for each part the organizations it is relevant to (several allowed; duplication is fine), the entries to **prune** as irrelevant to that organization, **redactions** (span → replacement, with a reason: disparaging or complaining about coworkers, career or job plans, personal life, investor or advisor talk, secrets), a relevance and confidence, and a one-line rationale per decision. The agent is free to overrule the evidence table: the table says where files changed, the agent decides whose work it was. Once publishing is on (`publish` in `destinations.json`, `off` by default; `archive publish on|off`), each part publishes to each named organization as a **derived snapshot** (lineage pointing at the source session and its entries). What isn't confidently some organization's stays personal only. A new revision re-runs the agent with the prior plan plus the new entries; a part whose plan changes is republished, and a part that no longer belongs is deleted from that organization. Failure (runner down, timeout, unparseable plan) holds the session; nothing publishes by default. Every plan and its rationale is stored and visible; low-confidence plans and every redaction go to a review queue; a person's override is a tag edit that survives re-capture and re-runs. The same agent runs once over the existing 1,172 sessions and recategorizes them, including deleting the already-leaked sessions from the UserEvidence Archive.

<!-- unit doc:docs/ROUTING.md#why-this-shape -->
**Source:** `docs/ROUTING.md` § Why this shape (in "Archive routing: an agentic pass over each session artifact (spec v2, Aron 2026-11-01; built)")

#### Why this shape

- Aron 11-01: "an agentic run on the session artifacts … to figure out where to put them, how to prune them, how to sanitize them, and if they're relevant"; "you can split up sessions"; "things can get duplicated … routed to multiple things if they're relevant"; Sonnet, "a single-digit percentage of your tokens"; the routing run itself "should not generate a session that we care about"; "recategorize things that you think are wrong". Earlier the same day: route by where the session is working, not where it started; Zealot → UE, inixiative GitHub → inixiative, else personal.
- Aron 10-31: default personal; work only when very convinced; sensitive stays personal or redacted; routing gets a review loop; touched-project routing isn't enough.
- Why the evidence table still matters: measured over 2,876 native transcripts (1,055 with tool calls), raw touches mislead (77's coordinator thread touched `~/code/zealot` 97 times, all reads, while building Zealot Wardens in Foundry), and the stripped text loses which repo files changed. Writes per organization are the one thing the agent can't recover from the artifact, so the store records them at ingest, before the strip.
- Cost, measured on the local Archive: the stripped artifacts total ~8.6M tokens across 1,172 sessions (events 5.0M, i.e. cross-session messages, notifications and subagent prompts; assistant 3.0M; user 0.5M). Median session ~1.3k tokens, p90 ~10k, p99 ~108k; 7 sessions over 150k get chunked. The one-time backfill is ~9M input tokens of Sonnet; steady state is new sessions plus deltas on revisions.

<!-- unit doc:docs/ROUTING.md#existing-primitives-reused-no-parallel-machinery -->
**Source:** `docs/ROUTING.md` § Existing primitives reused (no parallel machinery) (in "Archive routing: an agentic pass over each session artifact (spec v2, Aron 2026-11-01; built)")

#### Existing primitives reused (no parallel machinery)

| Concern | Primitive (path) | How / bridge |
|---|---|---|
| model runner, isolation, subscription | `suggest-claude.ts` (`ClaudePrimedSessions`, per-run dir under `decision-receipts/`, allowlisted env, user hooks/plugins off, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS`) | same runner, second charter; model Sonnet instead of the tagger's Haiku |
| suggestion + review loop | `suggest.ts` queue (`/suggestions/queue`, `/suggestions/record`), `suggestedTags` applied by a person; tag edits survive re-capture | plans are their own record (`RoutingPlan`) with rationale, reviewed in a queue like suggestions; override = tag edit |
| routing run not captured | run tags / exemption (`exemption.ts`), collector folder exclusions | the runner's directory is exempt the way the tagger's is; verify with a test that no routing run lands in the Archive |
| paths a tool call touches | `toolCallPaths`, `shellPaths`, `shellCommands` (`tags.ts`) | add a write-target mode to the same parser (one parser, two modes) |
| path → project → org | `projectPaths` (`tags.ts`), collector roots + worktrees (`collector.ts`), `routing.organizations` (`config.ts`) | unchanged; evidence counts come from the loop `projectTags` already runs |
| references | `archiveReferences` (`tags.ts`: "a link is not proof of work") | go into the evidence table, never route on their own |
| capture-time transform | `tool-activity.ts` strip at ingest | evidence computed before the strip, stored as a small record on the session |
| parts | `archiveLineageSchema` (`src/index.ts`, kinds `subagent \| fork \| part`, `parentSessionId`, `parentEntryId`) | the `part` kind carries the source entry range (`firstEntryId`, `lastEntryId`); a part is a derived snapshot, not a new model |
| routing → destinations | `sessionOrganizations` / `sessionDestinations` (`config.ts`), `publishArchive` digest-ack (`client.ts`) | input changes from "own + touched projects" to "the plan's parts × organizations"; publish path unchanged |
| removal | `/api/v1/archive/delete` (`server.ts`) | used when a re-plan drops a part, and for the backfill's leak cleanup |

<!-- unit doc:docs/ROUTING.md#cadence-aron-2026-11-01-replaces-after-30-min-idle -->
**Source:** `docs/ROUTING.md` § Cadence (Aron, 2026-11-01; replaces "after ~30 min idle") (in "Archive routing: an agentic pass over each session artifact (spec v2, Aron 2026-11-01; built)")

#### Cadence (Aron, 2026-11-01; replaces "after ~30 min idle")

The planner doesn't wait for a session to go idle. A host scheduler wakes every couple of minutes. It looks for sessions with new entries since their last plan, picks the ones due (each session at most about once an hour, with due times staggered so not everything runs at once), and spawns one planner run per due session. That run owns the session's plan. Each pass is a **delta**: the prior plan plus the entries added since it. A session that has paused, with no new entries for ~30 minutes, gets its pending delta planned at once, and the plan's version bumps. Published parts change version only when their plan changes.

<!-- unit doc:docs/ROUTING.md#as-built-2026-11-01-branch-feat-agentic-routing -->
**Source:** `docs/ROUTING.md` § As built (2026-11-01, branch `feat/agentic-routing`) (in "Archive routing: an agentic pass over each session artifact (spec v2, Aron 2026-11-01; built)")

#### As built (2026-11-01, branch `feat/agentic-routing`)

| Concern | Where |
|---|---|
| Evidence (write-target mode, one parser) | `src/tags.ts` `shellAccess` / `toolCallAccess`; `src/evidence.ts`; computed in `store.capture` before the strip, kept on the row (`evidence`, `evidenceKey`). A row no writer can re-send (transcript cleaned up, import, early Foundry thread) gets evidence from its stored snapshot when the host sends its map: start project and references only, under `stored:<key>`, so a returning transcript replaces it; the fill marks its plan due (`evidence`) |
| Project map (roots, worktrees, origin repos) | `agents.ts` `machineProjectMap` → `projects/set`; the collector sends each session's `cwd` |
| Parts | `src/parts.ts` `partSnapshot`; `store.applyParts` / `forgetDelivery`; lineage kind `part`; columns `partOf`, `routedTo` |
| Planner, validator | `src/route.ts` (`ROUTE_PROMPT`, `validatePlan`, `publishedParts`, `planSession`); `store.routingInput` / `recordPlan`; `RoutingPlan` table |
| Runner (isolated, pinned login) | `src/suggest-claude.ts` `claudeDecisionModel`, `claudeRouteModel`, `sweepDecisionRuns` |
| Scheduler | `store.routingDue`, `route.ts` `runRouting`, `archive route --watch`, `agents router` (LaunchAgent `com.inixiative.archive.route`) |
| Routing switch, delete on re-plan | `config.ts` `sessionOrganizations`; `client.ts` `syncArchives` deletion pass, `deleteRemote` |
| Backfill | `route.ts` `runBackfill`, `archive route --backfill [--dry-run]` |

**Review items.** B1: `validatePlan` (closed set, evidence per part, byte-exact redactions with a closed reason set and a fixed marker, foreign entries follow their own session, failure holds, confidence only orders the queue). B2: part ids `<sessionId>#part-<first entry id>`; one content per part (prunes and redactions are per part, not per organization, so one id never means two snapshots; a part that needs different content per organization is two parts); parts are local rows out of listings, search, suggestions and retention; they inherit `supersededBy`; the source never routes; `restore` lifts a direct destination's tombstone; receipts are forgotten on delete. B4: a subagent's evidence counts at its spawn entry in the parent, a subagent reaches only the parent's part at the spawn, and waits for the parent's plan. B5: exec cells' nested `exec_command` `workdir` and `apply_patch`. B6: evidence at `store.capture`, every writer; Foundry `{tool}` entries. S1: run directories name their process; dead runs and their primed transcripts are swept; close removes its own. S2: echoes of a redacted span are replaced across the part; the go-live read of 30 UE-bound parts is still to do. S3: sensitive personal parts, prunes and redactions are sticky; a person's `route:<org>` tag is ownership only (redaction still runs on new entries); `route reset` drops stickies. S4: plans are their own record; the planner runs on the host. S5: `gh --repo X` and `--repo=X`, `git --work-tree`, multi-file `sed -i`, `gh api` mutations, temp worktrees through registered roots. S6: the planner ignores `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and uses the default login; `organizations[].roster`. B3 (lens) deferred; B7 operational.

**Seams.** Kingdom: delete-on-replan calls `sessions.delete` with `{ documentId }`, per the Archive operation contract in `@inixiative/signet` (`src/archive.ts`); pairing asks for it. Kingdom's `sessions.write` has no `restore`, so a part deleted through Kingdom and later routed there again stays deleted at the hosted Archive until its content changes. Destinations running an Archive older than this branch refuse lineage kind `part`.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#routing -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Routing (in "Archive")

#### Routing

One archive per organization, not per project. `destinations.json` declares `organizations` (each an `id`, the `projects` it owns, a project belonging to at most one, and an optional `roster` of coworkers' names) and `destinations` (each naming its `organizationId`). There is no backwards compatibility: a `destinations.json` written before 0.23.0 (a bare list of destinations with `projectId`) is refused until it is rewritten in this shape.

**What publishes is a session's parts, as its routing plan says.** Every session is kept whole here (the personal Archive). A routing planner (below) cuts each session into **parts**, contiguous entry ranges, and gives each part the organizations whose work it is, several when it is work for each; anything not clearly some organization's stays personal, on this machine. A part is its own local row (`<sessionId>#part-<first entry id>`, lineage `kind: "part"` with `firstEntryId`/`lastEntryId`, `partOf` its session) holding the range's entries with the plan's prunes and redactions applied, its own title, no recorded references, only its organizations' `project:` tags and projectId, and never tool activity. The session itself publishes nowhere, and neither does a session with no plan yet or one whose plan was held: an unplanned session publishes nowhere. `project:` tags are for search only and never route. Parts stay out of local listings, search (`parts: "include" | "only"` asks for them), suggestions and retention, are superseded with their session, and go when it is deleted.

### 4b. Code entries

From the catalog (extracted from the code, described by a model). Each line: **name** `where` [kind] the job it does. Use: canonical usage.

#### Class `routing-planner`
- **claudeRouteModel** `src/suggest-claude.ts#claudeRouteModel` [primitive] run the routing planner on Sonnet, pinned to the default personal Claude login Use: claudeRouteModel(options) Reach: internal, not importable.
- **planSession** `src/route.ts#planSession` [primitive] plan one session's new entries: read what is needed, ask the model once, record the answer Use: await planSession(archive, model, archiveId) // called by runRouting Reach: internal, not importable.
- **publishedParts** `src/route.ts#publishedParts` [primitive] list the parts a valid plan publishes, leaving out pruned, sticky-sensitive or unrouted entries Use: publishedParts(plan, entries, foreign) Reach: internal, not importable (app code: `@inixiative/archive/store`).
- **runBackfill** `src/route.ts#runBackfill` [primitive] plan every session that has no plan yet, parents first, and report what each would publish Use: archive route --backfill [--dry-run] Reach: internal, not importable.
- **runRouting** `src/route.ts#runRouting` [primitive] run one scheduler pass planning every due session, a window at a time Use: archive route --watch (or the `agents router` LaunchAgent) Reach: internal, not importable.
- **validatePlan** `src/route.ts#validatePlan` [primitive] check a model's proposed plan against evidence in code, narrowing it, never widening Use: validatePlan(proposal, ...) // run by the store on recordPlan Reach: internal, not importable (app code: `@inixiative/archive/store`).

#### Class `routing-parts`
- **partSnapshot** `src/parts.ts#partSnapshot` [primitive] build a routed part as its own snapshot, with redactions applied and only its organizations' tags Use: partSnapshot(source, partSpec, redactions) Reach: internal, not importable (app code: `@inixiative/archive/store`).
- **redactText** `src/parts.ts#redactText` [primitive] replace every occurrence of every redacted span in a text, merging overlaps Use: redactText(text, redactions, { roster }) Reach: internal, not importable.
